title: Margaret Ekpo's birth chart
metaDescription: Margaret Ekpo's chart, computed from a sourced birth date: Sun at 3.6° Leo. Birth time unknown, so no houses or rising sign.
lede: The Sun stands at 3.6° Leo, in domicile — the planet in its own sign, running on home rules. Of everything the chart can be read for without a birth time, that is the loudest single fact in it.

blocks.title: Where the Sun actually stood
blocks.text: The Sun sits at 3.6° Leo — the first decan, 0°–10°, which the tradition sub-rules by the Sun. Degrees matter more than the sign label here: two people born a fortnight apart share Leo and share almost nothing else about where the Sun actually stood.

blocks.title: The personal registers
blocks.text: For the fast movers, Mercury was at 18.9° Cancer, Venus was at 13.8° Virgo, Mars was at 18.7° Virgo. Read together: a mind that absorbs before it argues; taste for the substantial and the lasting; drive that grinds rather than flares.

blocks.title: The angles that hold
blocks.text: Mercury and Mars hold the closest angle here — a sextile, 0.1° wide. The scheme reads a sextile as a door left unlocked. Useful, and entirely dependent on someone walking through it. Behind it, Saturn conjunction Pluto at 4.3°, and Venus conjunction Mars at 4.9° — both still well inside the orbs this site uses. Each angle here was measured at every hour of the civil day and held; whatever the missing clock said, this geometry was in it.

blocks.title: What the angles build
blocks.text: The Moon stands apart from every major angle the day held — the tradition reads an unaspected planet as a voice that speaks on its own schedule, unmodulated by the rest of the chart.

blocks.title: The classical map
blocks.text: The classical table has two entries for this chart. The Sun in Leo at 3.6° is in domicile — the planet in its own sign, running on home rules; Venus in Virgo at 13.8° is in fall — the tradition’s uphill placement, strength earned rather than given. None of these labels is a verdict on a person; they describe how a function is situated, nothing more.

blocks.title: The shape of the whole
blocks.text: The certain ground: 9 placements whose signs hold for the whole day, dividing 3 water, 3 air, 2 earth, 1 fire by element and 3 fixed, 3 cardinal, 3 mutable by mode. Water reads the room before the room speaks — atmosphere first, analysis later. Jupiter and Uranus were retrograde. Mercury changed direction during the day, so its motion is left open.

blocks.title: The Moon is genuinely open
blocks.text: The Moon crossed from Virgo into Libra during that day at the birthplace, travelling 14.2° between one midnight and the next. The hour would decide it; no hour was recorded. The reading keeps the question open rather than flipping a coin dressed as astrology.
